verdictRationale: The spec has strong safety principles, but it is not yet enforceable enough for implementation. The largest gaps are that manifests do not define the concrete file/artifact operations needed to generate a deterministic plan, and policy precedence remains ambiguous for customer installs without explicit policy.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A manifest advertises a package update with checksums but no canonical per-file paths or artifact digests, and the updater still produces an auto-apply plan.
falsifiability.observableSignal: The generated update-plan.json contains add_file or replace_generated_file operations whose source artifact, target path, and checksum cannot be traced to explicit manifest entries.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Run plan generation against a test manifest that contains only packages, migrations, and a generic checksums object, then inspect update-plan.json and assert every write operation has a canonical relative path, source digest, expected prior digest or nonexistence proof, and operation class.
falsifiability.threshold: zero write operations may be auto-apply eligible without explicit per-file manifest metadata

newIssueList.title: Manifest lacks enforceable file operation model
newIssueList.description: The spec requires deterministic planning, checksum verification for all changed files, generated-file ownership, and rollback snapshots, but the manifest schema only shows packages, migrations, a generic checksums object, and an optional signature. There is no canonical file list, artifact location, target path rule, prior checksum expectation, executable bit metadata, or ownership marker from which the updater can safely derive concrete operations. Under adversarial reading, different implementations could invent incompatible operation derivation rules while still claiming to satisfy the spec.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add a V1 manifest `files` or `artifacts` section with canonical relative target paths, content digests, artifact URIs or embedded source references, file mode, operation intent, generated ownership metadata, and optional expected prior digest. State that no file write can be planned unless it is backed by one explicit manifest entry.
newIssueList.lineRef: Update Manifest; Update Plan Generation; Acceptance Criteria 2-5

newIssueList.title: Customer no-policy default is contradictory
newIssueList.description: The spec says customer installs default to `stable` with `safe_additive` for templates, registries, and docs, but the Open Decisions section asks whether customer installs should default to `stable` or `pinned` when no explicit customer policy exists. It also says customer policy ambiguity is mitigated by requiring `UPDATE_POLICY.md` plus machine-readable local policy before apply. These statements leave the most safety-sensitive case, missing or incomplete customer policy, unresolved.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Make missing, unreadable, or conflicting customer policy fail closed for apply in v0, while still allowing `check`, `status`, and `heartbeat`. If a default is needed, define it as `pinned_version` until both machine-readable policy and human-readable policy are present and consistent.
newIssueList.lineRef: Channels And Defaults; Risks; Open Decisions

newIssueList.title: Approval gate artifact is underspecified
newIssueList.description: The spec repeatedly requires approval for risky, executable, permission-affecting, destructive, and customer-visible changes, but leaves the approval artifact format as an open decision. P2 and P3 behavior depends on knowing whether approval is a CLI token, signed file, or control-plane record, and what exactly it authorizes. Without this, an implementation might accidentally treat approval as broad permission to recompute or mutate a plan rather than permission to apply a specific precomputed plan.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define a minimal v0 approval artifact now: it should bind to root install_id, manifest digest, plan digest, operation ids, timestamp, approver identity string, and expiration. State that approval never authorizes operations absent from the approved plan digest.
newIssueList.lineRef: Apply Flow; P3 outputs; Risks; Open Decisions

newIssueList.title: Path safety rules are implicit
newIssueList.description: The spec forbids telemetry paths and emphasizes preserving local work, but it does not explicitly constrain update target paths. A malicious or malformed manifest could reference absolute paths, parent-directory traversal, symlinks, or files outside the OS root unless the path validation invariant is stated. Checksum verification alone does not prevent writing to the wrong location.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add path normalization rules: all manifest target paths must be relative to the OS root, must not contain `..`, must not be absolute, must not resolve through symlinks outside the root, and must be denied if they target secrets or local-only config unless explicitly approved.
newIssueList.lineRef: Update Manifest; Update Plan Generation; Apply Flow

preserveList.summary: The spec correctly narrows automatic apply to provable nonexistence, unchanged generated files, or deterministic additive registry merges.
The telemetry contract is substantially stronger than the rough idea because it requires an explicit allowlist and fail-closed behavior before sending.
The stale-plan re-gate before every write is a valuable invariant that directly protects operator edits made between planning and apply.
